When you connect to a service, you need a host name and a port number. In case of a web service, the first part of the URL contains he host name, and implicitly the protocol specifies the port number (port 80 for http and port 443 for https is the default but can be overridden in the URL).

"CONNECTION_REFUSED" is meaningless. It's like you sent a letter and it was "returned to sender" with no additional information. You don't know if the recipient is no longer at the address (incorrect IP in DNS). You don't know if the recipient's mailbox was knocked over (web server crashed, server is misconfigured, etc.) You don't know if someone along the delivery path blocked it (firewall). You just know that something kept it from being delivered (as opposed to a time out error where you're just guessing it wasn't delivered.)
